value: THERE IS A DEFECT CLASS NO SCORE IN THIS PROJECT CAN SEE, and one command now enumerates it image-wide. THE BLIND SPOT, four independent measurements of the same hole: (1) `fndiff --count` / `probe.py` `real` is computed by count_real(), which DROPS every line containing R_PPC -- so a relocation that names the wrong datum contributes nothing; (2) `fndiff --clean` scores reloc-NORMALIZED text, and normalized_reloc_lines collapses `lbl_*`, `jumptable*` and `@N` alike to `<local>` -- so a wrong pool symbol reads as MATCH; (3) `reloc_set_delta` keys both spellings through _reloc_key, which maps every local label to the string `<local>` too, so a TRANSPOSITION cancels perfectly in the multiset and the set delta is empty; (4) objdiff fuzzy scored game/enemy/enemy::damage_enemy at 99.2207% while our object loaded 0.0f where retail loads 1.0f. THE DETECTOR: tools/gdl/composed_census/es_named_reloc_census.py (promoted this run; run from the repo root, --out defaults to build/GUNE5D/es_named_census.json). For every NonMatching unit it aligns the two instruction streams with difflib on register-erased instruction text, and inside the matcher's EQUAL runs ONLY it pairs each instruction's relocations positionally, reporting the pairs where BOTH sides name a splitter `lbl_*` symbol and the names DIFFER. It then resolves each label's VALUE and SECTION through poolval.py so the row reads as data, not as hex. Rows are labelled TRANSPOSED (the same two labels appear on both sides, swapped -- a source operand or statement ORDER defect) or WRONG (not explained by a swap -- a wrong-constant / wrong-variable candidate). THE SOUNDNESS GATE IS THE WHOLE TOOL, and getting it wrong is measured, not theorised. Version 1 paired relocations by index across the whole function whenever the two instruction COUNTS were equal. game/mb/mb_model::MBOX_AllocModelMem is 102/102 with a 2-instruction schedule drift, and that version fabricated a row claiming we read a .sdata2 constant where retail reads a .sbss variable; the aligned view showed no such thing. Version 2 over-corrected by requiring the whole opcode SEQUENCE to agree, which reduced the census to 1 row and would have MISSED damage_enemy (whose multiset differs by a branch pair elsewhere in the body). Only the difflib EQUAL-run form is both sound and complete: 31 functions, measured 2026-09-03 at bc713b923. This is the same discipline fndiff --ops already applies to its IMMEDIATE rows, and the PAIRING UNRELIABLE banner it prints exists for exactly this failure. WORKED PROOF, game/enemy/enemy::damage_enemy: at +0x418 the target emits `lfs f0,0(0) @lbl_803468F0(EMB_SDA21)` and ours emitted `lfs f0,0(0) @lbl_80346820(EMB_SDA21)`. poolval: lbl_803468F0 = .sdata2 f32 1.0, lbl_80346820 = .sdata2 f32 0.0. The site is src/game/enemy/enemy.c:5349, the minimum-damage clamp `if (player_index >= 0 && (f64)amount < *(volatile f64*)&lbl_80346810 /* 1.0 */) amount = ...;`. Retail clamps sub-1.0 player damage UP TO 1.0; our reconstruction clamped it to 0.0, i.e. every player attack computing less than one point of damage did nothing. Fixed at commit 77b0aa9a4; real stayed 66 and fuzzy stayed 99.2207 -- the fix is INVISIBLE to every arbiter this project owns, which is the point of the law. SECOND FINDING FROM THE SAME CENSUS: game/world/camera::camera_mode_dest carried a clean 2x2 transposition, target `lfd f0,@lbl_803460B8`(180.0) / `lfd f2,@lbl_803460B0`(1/pi) against ours in the opposite order at both +0x34c and +0x394, i.e. our source wrote `(1/pi) * x * 180.0` where retail wrote `180.0 * x * (1/pi)`. Same value, different rounding, and the source-order swap took real 160 -> 158 with fuzzy 97.5499 -> 97.5645 (commit bc713b923). USAGE RULE, and it is not optional: a census row is a CANDIDATE, not a verdict. Confirm every row against `fnasm <unit> <fn> 0xA:0xB --diff` before editing, and read the ANONYMOUS side too -- game/mb/mb_blit::MBDrawBlits reported a WRONG row that is really a four-way permutation of hoisted constants in which two of the four are anonymous `@N` entries in our object (see attempt.mbdrawblits-hoisted-constant-deal-order-permutation.20260901.v1, which had already typed it correctly).
